record.context_brief: Removing topology assumptions for S2 area minimizers
record.original_question: On the two-sphere S^2, consider vector fields V of constant length r != 1 that are defined without boundary, and let Sigma_V be the associated surface in the sphere tangent bundle. The known area-minimization theorem assumes that Sigma_V is homeomorphic to a projective plane. Can this projective-plane topology assumption be removed while still concluding that the parallel-transport vector fields are the only area minimizers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^2$ denote the round unit 2-sphere and, for $r>0$ with $r\neq 1$, let $T^1 S^2(r)$ denote the bundle of tangent vectors to $S^2$ of constant length $r$, equipped with the Sasaki metric. Since $S^2$ admits no nowhere-vanishing continuous tangent vector field, by a "vector field of constant length $r$ without boundary" we mean a smooth map $V:U\to T S^2$ defined on a dense open set $U\subset S^2$ with $|V(p)|=r$ for all $p\in U$, such that the closure $\Sigma_V\subset T^1 S^2(r)$ of the image of $V$ is a surface without boundary. The area of $V$ is defined as the area of $\Sigma_V$ in $T^1 S^2(r)$.

A Pontryagin (parallel-transport) vector field is obtained by fixing a point $p_0\in S^2$ and a vector $v_0$ of length $r$ at $p_0$, and parallel-translating $v_0$ along every great circle through $p_0$; this yields a vector field defined on $S^2\setminus\{-p_0\}$ whose associated closed surface in $T^1 S^2(r)$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^2$.

It is known that if $V$ is a vector field of constant length $r\neq 1$ without boundary and $\Sigma_V$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^2$, then $V$ minimizes area among all such vector fields if and only if $V$ is a Pontryagin field.

Question: Does the same conclusion hold without the topological assumption that $\Sigma_V$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^2$? Equivalently, prove or disprove: every area-minimizing vector field of constant length $r\neq 1$ on $S^2$ (in the above sense) is a Pontryagin parallel-transport vector field.
artifact.status_search_result: The known characterization of area minimizers among constant-length vector fields on the round 2-sphere (Borrelli–Gil-Medrano and related works) is stated under the additional hypothesis that the associated surface in the unit tangent bundle is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{RP}^2$. Recent works (e.g., on Klein-bottle minimal surfaces in $T^1 S^2$ arising from area-minimizing unit fields on punctured spheres, and on vector field cycles in the tangent bundle) continue to assume or discuss this topological restriction, and no result removing the projective-plane assumption appears to have been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Area-minimizing vector fields on round 2-spheres (Borrelli–Gil-Medrano)
status_evidence.snippet: The only minimal surfaces of T^1 S^2(r) homeomorphic to the projective plane arising from vector fields without boundary are Pontryagin cycles.
status_evidence.claim: The original theorem requires the topology of Sigma_V to be RP^2.

status_evidence.title: Minimally Immersed Klein Bottles in the Unit Tangent Bundle of the Unit 2-Sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Area-minimizing unit vector fields on S^2 minus two points produce minimal Klein-bottle surfaces in T^1 S^2.
status_evidence.claim: Other topological types of minimal surfaces arise from related vector field problems, indicating that the RP^2 restriction is not automatic.

status_evidence.title: Vector Field Cycles in the Tangent Bundle (S. R. Simanca)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Pontryagin cycles and area minimization in unit tangent bundles of spheres.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to treat the problem and does not announce removal of the RP^2 hypothesis.
